sources.name: Flood Map for Planning (Rivers and Sea), Flood Zones 2 and 3
sources.publisher: Environment Agency, via the Defra Data Services Platform
sources.vintage: Live service; EA record last updated July 2026
sources.caveat: Modelled extent of flooding from rivers and the sea ignoring flood defences, so it overstates the risk where defences such as the Thames Barrier exist. Zone 3 is at least a 1 in 100 (rivers) or 1 in 200 (sea) yearly chance; Zone 2 here includes Zone 3 (at least 1 in 1,000). A share of the area, not of homes, and says nothing about any one property.

sources.name: Risk of Flooding from Surface Water (NaFRA2), high and medium likelihood
sources.publisher: Environment Agency, via the Defra Data Services Platform
sources.vintage: Live service; EA record last updated July 2026
sources.caveat: Modelled ponding from heavy rain: high is at least a 1 in 30 yearly chance, medium (as reported here) at least 1 in 100. Measured from 10 m map pixels, so figures are estimates. Drainage is only roughly represented; it flags where water collects, not which buildings flood.

sources.name: London Atmospheric Emissions Inventory (LAEI) 2022: modelled annual-mean concentrations (NO2, PM2.5, PM10)
sources.publisher: Greater London Authority (London Datastore), modelled by Ricardo / King's College London
sources.licence: Greater London Authority open data, London Datastore terms (typically UK OGL v3.0)
sources.vintage: Modelled for calendar year 2022 (published 2026); older than today
sources.caveat: A computer model of the whole city on a 20 m grid, not a measurement at your street. Each neighbourhood figure is the average of the grid cells inside it, so a busy road in an otherwise quiet area is smoothed out. It describes 2022, and traffic and fleet have changed since. WHO 2021 guideline values (NO2 10, PM2.5 5, PM10 15 ug/m3) are far stricter than the UK legal limits (NO2 40, PM10 40, PM2.5 20; England's PM2.5 target is 10 by 2040).
sources.attribution: Contains data from the London Atmospheric Emissions Inventory (LAEI 2022), © Greater London Authority.
